title: Attribution for merged request fan-in with cross-tenant batching and out-of-order delivery
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary:

In high-throughput serving, the runtime merges concurrent requests from multiple tenants into shared GPU batches (fan-in) to improve utilization. When responses are produced out-of-order (due to caching, KV-cache warmups, or retries) we currently lose precise per-tenant token attribution. This leads to incorrect quota enforcement, surprising rate-limit behavior, and occasional over/under billing for short-lived sessions.

Problem statement:
- Multiple independent sessions (tenants/users) are merged into the same execution batch. The runtime returns tokens as fragments which may be emitted non-deterministically relative to request arrival order.
- Retries and preemptions cause fragments to be re-sent or replayed.
- Current metering records final token counts using post-hoc heuristics and best-effort attribution, which misattributes tokens when ordering diverges.

Goal:
- Guarantee deterministic, auditable per-tenant token accounting for merged/fan-in batches while preserving batching benefits (latency/cost).
- Support correct quota checks, fair rate-limiting, and transparent billing for customers.

Proposed approach (snapshot-based provisional attribution):
1) Per-batch origin map: when the batch is constructed, capture a compact snapshot that maps batch slots to request origin (tenant_id, session_id, request_seq). Store this snapshot in the batch metadata store with an immutable batch_id.
2) Provisional credits at emit: when fragments are emitted (stream or sync), assign provisional token credits to origins using the snapshot. Tag each emitted frame with batch_id and slot_map references.
3) Finalize on completion/ack: only commit provisional credits to billing ledger after the request completion/terminal ack (or after a configured timeout). If a fragment is retried or re-emitted, use idempotency keys + sequence numbers to dedupe before committing.
4) Out-of-order correction window: if responses reorder, use snapshot to re-attribute fragment ownership deterministically (sequence number reconciliation) and adjust provisional credits before final commit.
5) Audit trail: persist provenance events (batch snapshot, emitted frames, retries, commit) to a write-once audit log for postmortem/billing reconciliation.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Storage: persisting batch snapshots and event logs increases storage and indexing cost; we'll garbage-collect snapshots after commit+retention window (default 30d).
- Latency: adding batch metadata and commit handshake may add a few ms to end-to-end path for very short requests; we must bench and gate this behind a feature flag.
- Consistency: provisional credits mean quotas reflect tentative usage until commit; choose conservative quota enforcement (deny only after commit) or hybrid (allow burst with provisional counters).

Design decisions taken so far:
- Use a compact binary-serializable slot map (not full request payloads) to keep snapshot size small (<= 1KB per batch typical).
- Commit-on-terminal-ack by default, with a configurable finalize-timeout (default 5s) to avoid indefinite provisional states for clients that disconnect.
- Idempotency: require incoming requests to provide idempotency-key for multi-frame streaming use-cases; runtime will synthesize if missing but will mark entry as 'non-idempotent' and use conservative crediting.

Open questions:
- How to enforce quotas during the provisional window without harming UX for low-risk customers? (Options: conservative enforcement / soft-limits / provisional reservation tokens).
- Retention policy for audit logs vs. compliance customers who need longer windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- No instances of cross-tenant token misattribution in unit/integration tests for fan-in scenarios.
- End-to-end benchmarks show <5% latency regression for 95th percentile on representative traces with feature enabled vs. baseline when batching sizes >4.
- Telemetry dashboards show provisional->committed credit ratios and any late re-attributions.
- Rollout plan and feature flag gating exist with ability to disable per-cluster.

testing_plan: Unit: serializer/deserializer for slot-map, dedupe logic, idempotency enforcement.
Integration: end-to-end fan-in simulation using test harness with deterministically reordered emits to verify attribution correctness.
Load: ramp to 10k concurrent sessions with mixed sync/stream clients to validate latency impact and GC behavior.
Chaos: network partitions between runtime and batch-metadata store to ensure commits time out and reconciliation works.
Billing-e2e: synthetic tenants with known token counts and injected reorders/retries to validate final ledger equality.
Audit: run reconciliation job to compare audit log commits to billing ledger; zero-tolerance for mismatch in test mode.
implementation_steps: 1. Add compact slot-map snapshot to batch builder and persist to batch-metadata store (runtime change)
2. Tag emitted stream frames with batch_id + slot indices and include provisional-credit markers (protocol change)
3. Implement provisional credit ledger and commit protocol in billing service; ensure atomicity with idempotency keys
4. Add GC and retention policy for snapshots + audit logs; expose retention config in Console
5. Add feature flag and per-cluster toggle with telemetry and dashboards
6. Run canary in staging with shadow billing and audit comparisons, then progressive rollout
